in_hebrew.name: יחטרה
in_hebrew.meaning: יחטרה הוא שם שפירושו יישועה או תושיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יחטרה הוא שם עברי שמקורו בכתבי הקודש, ופירושו הוא יישועה או תושיה. הוא קשור למושגים של ישועה והצלה, ויש לו קונוטציות רוחניות וחיוביות. השם יחטרה מופיע בכתבי הקודש כחלק מהמסורת היהודית והוא בעל חשיבות רבה בתרבות היהודית והנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ιεθρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιεθρα είναι ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος יחטרה, που σημαίνει σωτηρία ή σωσία. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Ιεθρα συνδέεται με έννοιες σωτηρίας και προστασίας, και έχει πνευματική σημασία για τους πιστούς.

in_latin.name: Jethra
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Jethra is derived from the Hebrew name יחטרה, which means salvation or deliverance. In the early Christian tradition, the name Jethra was associated with concepts of redemption and rescue, reflecting its biblical and spiritual significance.

in_english.name: Jethra
in_english.meaning: Jethra means salvation or deliverance in a spiritual context
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jethra originates from the Hebrew name יחטרה, meaning salvation or deliverance. In Christian tradition, Jethra symbolizes spiritual rescue and redemption. It carries connotations of hope, protection, and divine intervention. Historically, the name reflects the biblical themes of salvation and covenant.

biblical_reference.note: Jethra is mentioned as a son of Kohath in the biblical genealogies.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jethra, being derived from Hebrew, holds a rich cultural background in Judaism and Christianity. It is suggestive of a divine or God-given presence and is often associated with gifts and blessings. In the Christian world, such a name could be a powerful reminder of the idea that every human being is a unique creation of God and a bearer of His image and likeness.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Jethra can serve as a reminder of the biblical principle of stewardship, which recognizes all blessings - including talents, intellect, and physical abilities - as gifts from God. It also underscores the belief in the Christian faith that every person has inherent worth and value, bestowed upon them directly by God. In essence, Jethra can be a daily reminder of the divine source of our very being and the obligations that come with being a recipient of such a profound gift.

historical_references.reference: Jethra was a priestess and the daughter of Jerubbaal, the second judge of Israel. She played a role in the story of Gideon, who was chosen by God to save Israel from the Midianites. Jethra tried to discourage Gideon from leading the Israelites to battle, but he remained steadfast in his faith.

Another reference to Jethra can be found in the New Testament book of Acts, where she is mentioned as one of the initial converts to Christianity in the city of Damascus. She was a wealthy merchant and played a significant role in the early spread of the faith in that region.
